Subject: Post-demo: quantization tradeoffs + model fit  FinWave next steps

Hi Sam / Priya

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Great to see the ingestion pipeline and the examples you shared for risk memo summarization  very helpful context. Quick recap and clear next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary workload: summarization + relevance reranking for regulatory memos (avg doc length ~2.5k tokens; peak ~12k).
- SLOs: P99 latency target ~1.2s for single-pass summarization endpoint; batch jobs can be slower.
- Concern: model quality regression when applying aggressive quantization for cost reasons.

Recommended immediate workstreams (our proposed order):
1) Model fit evals  run candidate models (LlamaX-13B, Redstone-7B, Redstone-13B) on your prompt set and compare abstractive quality on your eval metrics (ROUGE/ROUGE-L, factuality checks).
2) Quantization trade study  AWQ 4-bit vs GPTQ 4-bit vs FP8 (dynamic) focusing on latency, memory, and quality delta for your prompts.
3) Throughput tuning  batching and KV cache settings for the long-doc path to preserve latency SLOs.

Deliverables we can provide by next Tue (6/29):
- Eval report: per-model quality deltas and recommended model for production.
- Tradeoff spreadsheet: latency/cost/quality for AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 with sample configs.
- Prompt set and a reproducible eval harness (we'll share the Drive folder).

Attachments included: finwave_prompt_set_v1.csv (your sample prompts + expected outputs), benchmarks/finwave_latency_cost_breakdown.csv (sample numbers from our internal runs), redwood_awq_vs_gptq_summary.pdf (summary of tradeoffs). Also shared a Drive folder link below.

Questions for you:
- Do you have a hard constraint on token-level cost (e.g., budget target per 10k requests/month)?
- For the long-doc summarization, is progressive extract-then-abstractive ok (we suggested prefix extraction to keep generation tokens down)?

Next call suggestion: Wed 6/30 11:00am PT  30m to review the first eval pass and pick a candidate for a 2-week pilot.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa  super helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Budget: we are aiming to keep inference compute under $8k/month for the initial pilot (normalize to tokens/month if needed).
2) Quality tolerance: for abstraction we need >=95% parity on entity preservation and <=5% increase in hallucination rate versus your baseline (we can share our evaluation rubric).

On quantization: our infra team is wary of AWQ because of reports of small, but noticeable, hallucination increases on instruction-heavy prompts. Would be great to see per-prompt deltas rather than averages.

Also, Priya wants to loop in Procurement early for the pilot contract (Procurement contact is priya.desai@finwave.com).

Confirming Wed 6/30 11:00am PT works for us.

Great, thanks Sam  noted on the $8k pilot target and the strict quality thresholds. We'll make sure the evals include per-prompt breakdowns and hallucination-focused checks. Quick notes on the trade study approach so expectations are clear: 

Trade study plan (high level):
- Models: Redstone-13B (FP16 baseline), Redstone-13B-AWQ (4-bit), Redstone-13B-GPTQ (4-bit), LlamaX-13B (FP16 and AWQ).
- Metrics: ROUGE-L, factuality score (automated NER/number-check diffs), hallucination delta (human spot checks on 40 examples), latency P50/P95/P99, memory footprint, and per-1000-request cost estimate.
- Per-prompt analysis: we'll produce a CSV with rows per prompt and columns for quality metrics so you can identify specific prompt classes that regress under quantization.

Early observations from our sandbox (attached summary):
- AWQ (aggressive 4-bit) often gives best memory/latency but can show small regressions on instruction-following items  the effect is prompt-dependent and concentrated on longer, multi-step instructions.
- GPTQ 4-bit tends to preserve generative behavior better on instruction prompts but with slightly higher memory and latency than AWQ.
- FP8 dynamic shows promise for matching FP16 quality with reduced memory on supported hardware, but runtime support is more limited and we may see variability across GPU types.

Suggested guardrails for pilot:
- Start pilot on GPTQ 4-bit for the production endpoint and run a shadow AWQ config to measure regression in parallel (can automatically roll back if hallucination delta exceeds threshold).
- Keep a small subset (5-10%) of traffic on FP16 baseline for continuous quality monitoring.

Action items we will take by Tue 6/29:
- Share the per-prompt eval CSV and a one-page recommendation for pilot config.
- Provide a sample runtime config for GPTQ 4-bit + batching settings tuned to your P99 SLO.

Rishi / Jonas  can you confirm we have the right template for the hallucination checks (human spot-check plan) and whether we want vendor-signed SOC evidence included in the pilot deliverables?

-Marissa
